process_checkpoint.scope: Confirmed-write subcase: original isolated Store/worker wrote and confirmed a pending checkpoint before full process force-stop. New PID reopened, committed once and confirmed canonical replacement before a second force-stop. Third PID reopened exact canonical bytes. Synthetic input/owner fault; no manually seeded checkpoint, partial-write kill, power loss or ordinary UI claim. The separate undelivered_completion subcase records visible worker bytes before owner delivery.

undelivered_completion.scope: Original worker new canonical bytes were visible while the main owner was blocked inside its save action with zero callbacks and an in-flight ledger. Full process force-stop before owner delivery; new PID reopened the exact two-stroke canonical root. Not a partial-write or power-loss test.
